subject: Operator escrow, install runbook, and telemetry exhibit for on-prem/private deploy

Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator escrow, install runbook, and telemetry exhibit for on-prem/private deploy

Irene,

Thanks for taking our inbound on this. As part of our procurement and security review for the private deployment (Vanguard Health production cluster), we need the following evidence to move to the vendor-security board next week: 

- Operator credential escrow options (matrix of approaches you support: customer-managed KMS, HSM-based escrow, shared vault escrow, hardware token workflow). Please indicate which you recommend for air-gapped installs.
- Installation runbook (step-by-step high level + operator prerequisites, expected MOP time, rollback), ideally a redacted PDF or playbook we can share with our on-call teams.
- Sample telemetry/telemetry manifest (what signals you collect during install and runtime, retention defaults, PII-minimization steps). If possible include a short 24h log snippet showing typical agent heartbeats and KV cache metrics (sanitized).
- A short statement on what you will and will not provide as part of the escrow package (private keys, operator secrets, credentials).

Procurement will also need any standard template or SOW language that references operator access controls and escrow responsibilities. Can you confirm you can deliver the items above by EOD tomorrow (May 31)? If not, please advise the earliest possible ETA. 

Signe
Signe Moller
Director, Infrastructure Security
Vanguard Health

---
Attachment request: please mark any attached files with version/date and include digest/hash if available.
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Signe Moller <signe.moller@vanguard-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator escrow, install runbook, and telemetry exhibit for on-prem/private deploy

Hi Signe — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a package that covers each item. I’ve attached three artifacts (stubs) to this reply: redwood_install_runbook_v1.pdf, operator-escrow-matrix.xlsx, and telemetry-sample-24h.log. Summary below.

Quick summary of attachments:
- redwood_install_runbook_v1.pdf — high-level operator runbook with pre-install checklist, network assumptions, operator prerequisites, step-by-step install (air-gapped and VPC modes), common failure modes, and rollback steps. Sensitive operational secrets are redacted; the runbook references customer-managed KMS pattern for secret injection.
- operator-escrow-matrix.xlsx — matrix comparing options (customer-managed KMS, HSM escrow, sealed hardware tokens, company-managed escrow with attestation). The file includes recommended defaults and a short notes column about the tradeoffs for air-gapped scenarios.
- telemetry-sample-24h.log — sanitized 24-hour agent log excerpt showing heartbeat, KV cache hit/miss rates, and install-time resource utilization. No customer PII included.

Couple clarifying questions so we deliver the exact scope you need:
1) For the escrow: do you require physical custody (hardware tokens deposited with a third party) or a cryptographic escrow (encrypted key blob held off-site)? We can produce language for either approach.
2) Retention: what is your target for operator telemetry retention (30/90/365 days)? We’ll include guidance for each.

If we’re aligned I’ll also route a short legal/engineering blurb for the procurement team describing what Redwood will never escrow (e.g., private master signing keys for our service, licensing entitlements).

Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_install_runbook_v1.pdf (redacted), operator-escrow-matrix.xlsx, telemetry-sample-24h.log
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Signe Moller <signe.moller@vanguard-health.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator escrow, install runbook, and telemetry exhibit for on-prem/private deploy

Signe — following up with some technical notes and the escrow/telemetry constraints we discussed internally. I’ve attached the operator-escrow-matrix.xlsx (v1.1) and included inline highlights below.

Escrow options (high level):
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended): Redwood supports injecting operator credentials at runtime via a customer-provided KMS (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Key Vault / on-prem PKCS#11). Pros: keys never transit our control plane; works in both VPC and fully air-gapped installs. Cons: customer must expose an agent-accessible KMS endpoint during install or provide sealed blobs.
- HSM-based escrow: We can ship encrypted credential blobs bound to an HSM attestation key. For air-gapped installs, the customer must have a compatible HSM or accept on-prem hardware token handover.
- Hardware token (physical escrow): For highest assurance, tokens are created and deposited with an escrow agent. This is slower but satisfies physical custody requirements.

What we will not escrow:
- Redwood platform master signing keys, private model weights that are licensed under third-party agreements, or secrets used for Redwood internal telemetry aggregation.

Telemetry manifest summary:
- Collected signals during install: agent start/stop, controller KV-cache metrics, certificate handshake attempts, network egress attempts, package verification events. All logs are timestamped and include a component tag.
- Default retention: 30 days for full verbosity, 365 days aggregated metrics. We can configure to 90/365 for contract terms.
- PII minimization: never collect full user payloads or customer prompt content. Telemetry is scoped to operational telemetry only.

Sanitization note: the attached telemetry-sample-24h.log is scrubbed. If you need field-level hashes for log integrity we can provide SHA256 digests for each file.

Next steps: Irene — if Vanguard confirms physical escrow vs. cryptographic escrow preference and a retention target, Ben and I will produce the procurement clause and an annex to the SOW. Happy to join a short technical session if your team prefers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator-escrow-matrix.xlsx (v1.1), telemetry-sample-24h.log (sanitized)

Irene / Ben — received, thanks. The artifacts look good from a preliminary review. A few quick items: 

- We will aim for cryptographic escrow (customer-managed KMS) for initial install, with a secondary option for hardware-token custody if our compliance team requests physical escrow at approval.
- Retention target: 90 days for full verbosity, 365 days aggregated metrics. Please include a short paragraph in the SOW annex describing retention change windows and deletion procedures.

Procurement requests a 30-minute technical workshop tomorrow (May 31) at 11:00 AM PT to walk through the runbook and the KMS integration steps. Can you confirm a Redwood engineer for that slot? If you prefer a different time, let us know.

Also, procurement attached the internal intake ID: VG-INTAKE-4892 (refer to this in the SOW annex).

Signe
